task_description: Write a method in Dafny to find the length of the smallest list in a list of lists.
specification_response:
method LengthOfSmallestList(lists: seq<seq<int>>) returns (length: nat)
Postconditions_prompt:
    - The returned value is equal to the length of one of the non-empty lists within the input list of lists
    - If all lists are empty, the returned value is 0
    - The returned value is less than or equal to the length of every list in the input sequence
code_response:
Step 1: Determine the method’s signature.
In this case:
    method MinListLength(lists: seq<seq<int>>) returns (minLength: int)

Step 2: Determine the preconditions.
In this case:
Natural language description:
    - The list of lists should not be empty; i.e., there should be at least one list
    - Each inner list can be empty or non-empty, but the outer list must contain at least one inner list

Dafny specification:
    requires |lists| > 0

Step 3: Determine the postconditions.
In this case:
Natural language description:
    - The returned value is the length of the smallest inner list in the list of lists

Dafny specification:
    ensures minLength >= 0
    ensures exists i :: 0 <= i < |lists| && minLength == |lists[i]|

Step 4: Write the code, its formal specification, and the verification annotations that help the solver prove the postconditions.
In this case:

```dafny
method MinListLength(lists: seq<seq<int>>) returns (minLength: int)
    requires |lists| > 0
    ensures minLength >= 0
    ensures exists i :: 0 <= i < |lists| && minLength == |lists[i]|
{
    // Initialize minLength with the length of the first inner list
    minLength := |lists[0]|;
    // Loop over all inner lists to find the minimum length
    var i := 1;
    while i < |lists|
        invariant 1 <= i <= |lists|
        invariant minLength >= 0
        invariant exists j :: 0 <= j < i && minLength == |lists[j]|
    {
        if |lists[i]| < minLength {
            minLength := |lists[i]|;
        }
        i := i + 1;
    }
}
```
